text:
maria: quick heads-up — follow-up from the rollout RFC: we need a concrete proposal for tenant-scoped canaries + automatic fallbacks.
maria: current pain: global canaries are noisy for high-variance tenants. want per-tenant risk budgets so we don't blow up a single customer's p95.
josh: agree. proposal: attach a small 'risk_budget' to tenant metadata (eg 0.5% errors / 10m) and have the router consume budget when a new variant is in flight.
tariq: how do we track errors vs budget? count 5xx + high-latency responses as budget drains?
sophia: +1 to combining latency and error. need weighting: latency spikes should be allowed short bursts but persistent spikes deduct more.
maria: rough state machine: START -> TRIAL (x% traffic) -> OBSERVE (metrics window) -> PROMOTE or ROLLBACK. Budget prevents TRIAL if budget exhausted.
kevin_oncall: add requirement: automatic rollback must create an incident ticket if rollback happens during business hours. we need notifications.
deploy-bot: deploy started for variant v2 on canary group tenant:acme-corp
josh: interface boundary thought: router only needs a boolean from policy engine: allow_canary(tenant, variant, sample_id) -> {allow, reason}. policy engine returns 'defer' too.
tariq: keep router side simple. policy engine should be stateful (track windows, budgets, counters). router caches decisions for short TTL.
sophia: observability: emit these events: canary.start, canary.decision, canary.metrics.window, canary.rollback. include tags: tenant, variant, decision_reason, budget_remaining.
maria: example policy config (WIP):
```
canary_policy:
  sample_fraction: 0.01
  min_traffic: 5
  metrics_window: 300s
  risk_budget:
    errors: 0.005   # fraction
    latency_p95_increase_ms: 200
  thresholds:
    error_rate: 0.01
    p95_multiplier: 1.5
```
josh: fallback hierarchy: 1) retry on same variant, 2) route to stable variant, 3) route to lighter quantized variant, 4) fall back to cached response or degrade gracefully.
tariq: important: ensure KV cache keys include variant id so cached responses don't leak between variants.
kevin_oncall: what about cross-tenant spillover when routing to stable? need throttling so one tenant's rollback doesn't backpressure stable pool.
sophia: add circuit-breaker per-tenant on stable target, and global slow-path queue with rate limits.
maria: tradeoffs: having policy engine centrally gives better global view but is a single point of failure. alternative: shard policy by tenant, replicate state to avoid SPOF.
josh: suggestion: hybrid — local policy cache in router with periodic sync + write-through to central policy for counters.
tariq: failure modes list:
- policy sync lag -> inconsistent canary decisions
- budget miscalc on time drift -> accidental over-rollout
- metric ingestion lag -> delayed rollback
- router cache poisoning -> wrong routing
maria: mitigations: monotonic counters, versioned policy blobs, safeties: hard-stop global kill-switch and default to stable variant when uncertain.
kevin_oncall: SLA note: any automatic rollback must preserve invariant: no increased error budget consumption for stable traffic. logging must be searchable by tenant+window.
deploy-bot: rollback executed for variant v2 on tenant:acme-corp at 1860001400
josh: follow-ups: I'll draft the policy API spec and a minimal proto for allow_canary. maria, can you take the budget semantics and failure-mode appendix?
maria: yep — will draft and link to RFC. can we set a short sync meeting tomorrow 09:30? :calendar:
tariq: I'll add oncall runbook snippets for automatic rollback path.
sophia: I'll add the observability event contract to ops-dashboards.
kevin_oncall: tagging SRE + Platform for review. good discussion. :thumbsup:
